notes: With-skill achieves 100% pass rate across all 3 evals (15/15 assertions) vs 67% without skill (10/15)

The 3 assertions that discriminate most: 'model bag warning' (with: 3/3 pass, without: 1/3), 'evaluates architecture first' (with: 3/3, without: 2/3), 'acknowledges app type' (with: 3/3, without: 1/3)
Eval 3 (package manager) shows the largest gap: skill explicitly names and explains anti-patterns; baseline creates the exact anti-pattern it should warn about
With-skill runs use ~37% more tokens (reading skill + references) and take ~22% longer, but the quality improvement is substantial
Both with and without skill correctly reject model/service/io for package managers and correctly split god modules for web APIs — the baseline is not bad, the skill just catches more edge cases
